full_judgment: 7. Further case of the defendant No. 1 was that the defendant No. 1 was a doctor who held a dispensary in a room of the suit building. The defendant No. 1 himself also erected two small tin shed huts in the suit land and leased out the same to the tenants who installed a betel shop and a cycle mending shop at a monthly rental shop. The contesting defendant No. 1 has also pleaded that the East Bengal Mercantile Bank was not an agriculturist and no agriculture income tax was imposed upon it. The plaintiff collusively filed a certificate case against the Bank in complicity with the certificate officer with a malafide intention to grab the suit property. No notice was served upon the certificate debtors in accordance with law. Moreover, sale proclamation and the sale certificate were confined to selling the buildings and doors and windows of the buildings on the suit land and that the land was not advertised for sale in the proclamation of sale. That the plaintiff purchased the buildings and doors and windows of the buildings in that auction, that the certificate officer being gained over by the plaintiff ousted the defendant No. 1 and his family from the suit property by illegal force and as such the defendant No. 1 filed Other Class Suit No. 17 of 1961 under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act in the 4th Court of the Subordinate Judge, Mymensingh for restoration of possession of the suit building and land measuring 12 decimals out of the suit property and the said suit was decreed upto the Supreme Court. The defendant No. 1 filed the Execution Case No. 4 of 1961 for execution of the said decree. The plaintiff has filed the instant suit to delay of the said execution case. The defendant No. 1 was a tenant under East Bengal Mercantile Bank and he became owner of the suit property after acquisition of the rent receiving interest under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. That the plaintiff did not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land by his alleged purchase of the same in auction. The suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.
